lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Guided practice: cost and funding in outline, verified not assumed

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic cost and funding in outline, verified not assumed task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner researches, at the category level, what a pathway typically costs (tuition, fees, tools, licensing, lost income, and similar) and what kinds of funding or aid categories typically exist for it (scholarships, grants, employer-paid training, tuition assistance, and similar), without looking up or recording any real dollar figures tied to their own household.
safetyNotes: This lesson works at the level of general cost and funding categories only; the learner does not look up or record any real family income, savings, debt, or other household financial detail.
No account is created and no application or form is submitted anywhere for this lesson.
materials: learner-local: access to look up general program cost and aid information

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g11-u01-l03-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g11-u01-l03-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g11-u01-l03-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g11-u01-l03-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Based on this outline, what is one specific question about cost or funding you would still need to research further before this pathway felt fully realistic?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g11-u01-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g11-u01-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g11-u01-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Category accuracy for cost: At least three specific, pathway-appropriate cost categories are named for each pathway. | Category accuracy for funding: At least two specific funding or aid categories are named per pathway, each with a source. | Staying at the category level: Response stays entirely at the general category level with no real personal financial detail. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u01-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner pick one funding category they listed and research one specific, real eligibility rule for it (such as a deadline type or a qualifying condition), recording the category-level rule without needing any personal financial figures.

resources.title: cost and funding in outline, verified not assumed coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner researches, at the category level, what a pathway typically costs (tuition, fees, tools, licensing, lost income, and similar) and what kinds of funding or aid categories typically exist for it (scholarships, grants, employer-paid training, tuition assistance, and similar), without looking up or recording any real dollar figures tied to their own household.
Coach direction: Before researching, write down what cost and funding categories you currently assume exist for each of your two pathways.
Learner prompt: For your two pathways, what kinds of costs and what kinds of funding or aid do you currently assume exist, even if you're not sure they're accurate?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: cost and funding in outline, verified not assumed complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Research and list the general categories of cost that typically apply to each pathway.
Response 1 (t2-p1): For each pathway, list the general categories of cost that typically apply (for example: tuition, fees, tools or equipment, licensing or testing fees, lost income while training).
Response 2 (t2-p2): My cost categories are general categories, not real dollar amounts tied to my own household.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: cost and funding in outline, verified not assumed minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Based on this outline, what is one specific question about cost or funding you would still need to research further before this pathway felt fully realistic?

Success checks: Category accuracy for cost: At least three specific, pathway-appropriate cost categories are named for each pathway. | Category accuracy for funding: At least two specific funding or aid categories are named per pathway, each with a source. | Staying at the category level: Response stays entirely at the general category level with no real personal financial detail.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: cost and funding in outline, verified not assumed supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g11-u01-l03-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g11-u01-l03-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional cost and funding in outline, verified not assumed condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Category accuracy for cost: At least three specific, pathway-appropriate cost categories are named for each pathway. | Category accuracy for funding: At least two specific funding or aid categories are named per pathway, each with a source. | Staying at the category level: Response stays entirely at the general category level with no real personal financial detail..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u01-l03-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
